Tests: tests/api/ledger-controls.test.ts (permission matrix over 8 roles for all four new permissions, 22 cases), tests/api/permissions.test.ts (4 new probes x 8 roles), packages/contracts/src/ledger.test.ts
rows.accept: Only holders of the permission can post OPENING_BALANCE; owner/admin/partner hold it, others do not; 403 and audited denial otherwise; role/permission sync tests pass.

rows.req: Control accounts protected from ordinary manual postings; narrowly authorised adjustments need reason, evidence and audit trail
rows.ev: CONTROL_ADJUSTMENT request needs `ledger:control-adjustment` (accountant, owner/admin/partner), a reason of at least 20 characters (service + database check), at least one evidence document that exists, belongs to the company and is readable by the requester (restricted documents indistinguishable from missing), and must touch a control account. The journal records request, requester and approver and the evidence is linked journal -> document in the evidence graph; MANUAL journals still refused on control accounts. Tests: tests/api/ledger-controls.test.ts (validation, control-account adjustment, evidence graph), tests/platform/posting-service.test.ts
rows.accept: A CONTROL_ADJUSTMENT request needs permission `ledger:control-adjustment`, a reason of at least 20 characters and at least one evidence document readable by the requester; posting without them fails; the journal links to the request, the evidence and the approver; ordinary MANUAL journals still cannot touch control accounts.

rows.req: Configurable second-person approval for material opening balances and exceptional control-account adjustments
rows.ev: Per-company `ledger_policy` (ALWAYS default / ABOVE_THRESHOLD with strictly-greater materiality threshold, expiry 1-90 days; no NEVER mode - database check). Above the threshold a different person holding `ledger:approve` must approve; requester can never approve (service + database, tested against the table owner path). Below-threshold direct posting only when configured, recorded as self-approved; reject (reason required), cancel (requester only) and expiry leave the ledger untouched. Policy changes need `ledger:policy` + reason and are audited before/after. Tests: tests/api/ledger-controls.test.ts (policy, threshold boundary 1000.00 / 1000.01, concurrency), tests/db/ledger-controls.test.ts (13), tests/platform/ledger-requests.test.ts (5)
rows.accept: Per-company policy sets the materiality threshold and which request kinds need approval; above it the journal is not posted until a different person holding `ledger:approve` approves; the requester can never approve their own request; below the threshold policy may allow direct posting only if configured; approval posts through the PostingService; rejection and expiry leave the ledger untouched.
rows.deferred: Per-account rules; delegation; multi-step chains

rows.req: Approval requests are not ledger entries: pending requests cannot affect balances; posted journals stay immutable; correction by reversal only
rows.ev: Pending requests live in `journal_request` and are never read by trial balance / general ledger (asserted). An approved request produces exactly one journal (unique `journal.request_id`; idempotency key `request:<id>`; concurrent approvals and approve/reject/cancel races end with one outcome). Posted journals stay immutable and are corrected by reversal (tested); AI actors cannot request, approve or post (service + PostingService). Request content is immutable and decided requests final (trigger); no delete/truncate for runtime role or owner. Tests: tests/api/ledger-controls.test.ts, tests/db/ledger-controls.test.ts, tests/platform/ledger-requests.test.ts, tests/db/privileges.test.ts, tests/unit/architecture.test.ts (single writer of journal_request/ledger_policy)
rows.accept: Trial balance and general ledger ignore pending requests; an approved request produces exactly one journal (idempotent); tests prove no UPDATE/DELETE path; the AI actor cannot request or approve.

rows.accept: The first-day-of-first-period rule remains; a test shows the permission, approval and date rule all apply together.

rows.req: Exchange-rate source and date: rates stored with source, rate date, provenance and verification status; lookup rule documented
